newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish business group demands tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: Polish business group demands tax cuts.

text.p: A Polish business group demanded on Thursday that personal income and corporate tax be significantly lowered to boost economic activity.

The group, called the 1998 Tax Coalition and including several dozen employers and business executive groups, said it wanted a cut next year of the highest personal income tax bracket to 32 percent from the current 44 percent.

The group, consisting of such organisations as the Business Centre Club (BCC) and the Polish Employers Confederation (KPP), also said it wanted the corporate tax to be lowered to 32 percent next year from the current 38 percent.

"A one-off lowering of the highest tax bracket for individuals and firms will boost business activity and reduce the economy's grey sphere, but it will not lower the budget's revenues," group head Witold Michalek told a news conference, referring to economic activity illegally untaxed.

Parliament ruled in 1996 that next year the personal income tax levels will decrease to 19, 30 and 40 percent, depending on income, from this year's 20, 32, and 44 percent. The corporate tax is to gradually be lowered to 32 percent by the year 2000.
The current government, grouping ex-communists and a peasant party, plans no change to the regulation. @
Some members of right-wing and centrist oppostion groups, present at the news conference, said they supported the proposal to cut taxes.
